# bioexcel/biobb_mem/mda_hole

## Summary

Wrapper of the MDAnalysis HOLE module for analyzing ion channel pores or transporter pathways.

MDAnalysis HOLE provides an interface to the HOLE suite of tools to analyze pore dimensions and properties along a channel or transporter pathway. The parameter names and defaults follow the MDAnalysis HOLE implementation.

Nextflow adapter of the [MDAHole](https://biobb-mem.readthedocs.io/en/latest/mdanalysis_biobb.html#module-mdanalysis_biobb.mda_hole) building block of [biobb_mem](https://github.com/bioexcel/biobb_mem) 5.3.1.

## Get started

```nextflow
include { BIOBB_MEM_MDA_HOLE } from 'bioexcel/biobb_mem/mda_hole'

workflow {
    BIOBB_MEM_MDA_HOLE(ch_input)
}
```

Optional input files are passed as `[]`.

## Inputs

| Name | Required | Formats | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `meta` | yes | | Map with at least an `id` key, used as tag and output file prefix |
| `input_top_path` | yes | crd, gro, mdcrd, mol2, pdb, pdbqt, prmtop, psf, top, tpr, xml, xyz | Path to the input structure or topology file |
| `input_traj_path` | yes | arc, crd, dcd, ent, gro, inpcrd, mdcrd, mol2, nc, pdb, pdbqt, restrt, tng, trr, xtc, xyz | Path to the input trajectory to be processed |

## Outputs

Each output channel emits `[meta, file]`. Files are named `<prefix>_<role>.<extension>`, where role is the output argument without `output_` and `_path`.
Optional outputs are only produced if requested in `ext.outputs`.

| Channel | Required | Formats (default first) | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `output_hole_path` | yes | vmd | Path to the output HOLE analysis results |
| `output_csv_path` | yes | csv | Path to the output CSV file containing the radius and coordinates of the pore |
| `versions_biobb_mem` | yes | | `[process, 'biobb_mem', version]`, also sent to the `versions` topic |

## Configuration

Set with `ext` in a `process` `withName` selector:

| Option | Description |
|---|---|
| `ext.properties` | Map of MDAHole properties (see below). Defaults: `[can_write_file_log: false]` |
| `ext.outputs` | Map of output argument to extension, for example `[output_hole_path: 'vmd']`. Required outputs use their first format by default; optional outputs are only requested when listed here |
| `ext.prefix` | Output file prefix (default: `meta.id`) |

`raise_error` and `restart` are always set by the adapter: failed commands fail the task, and `-resume` replaces restart.
Do not set the `container_*` properties: Nextflow runs the task inside the biobb_mem container.

```groovy
process {
    withName: 'BIOBB_MEM_MDA_HOLE' {
        ext.properties = [executable: 'hole']
    }
}
```

### Properties

| Name | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `start` | integer | null | Starting frame for slicing. |
| `stop` | integer | null | Ending frame for slicing. |
| `steps` | integer | null | Step for slicing. |
| `executable` | string | "hole" | Path to the HOLE executable. |
| `select` | string | "protein" | The selection string to create an atom selection that the HOLE analysis is applied to. |
| `cpoint` | array | null | Coordinates of a point inside the pore (Å). If None, tries to guess based on the geometry. |
| `cvect` | array | null | Search direction vector. If None, tries to guess based on the geometry. |
| `sample` | number | 0.2 | Distance of sample points in Å. This value determines how many points in the pore profile are calculated. |
| `end_radius` | number | 22.0 | Radius in Å, which is considered to be the end of the pore. |
| `dot_density` | integer | 15 | Density of facets for generating a 3D pore representation. |
| `remove_tmp` | boolean | true | Remove temporal files. |
| `sandbox_path` | string | "./" | Parent path to the sandbox directory. |
